newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal rate move seen only after April CPI.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal rate move seen only after April CPI.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal has room to cut its key intervention rates on Friday but it is more likely to wait until after April inflation figures before making a move, analysts said.

They said the escudo's recent strength gave the central bank the scope for a rate cut but a short-term liquidity squeeze in the money market and the consumer price data, which is due by mid-May, meant it was unlikely the Bank would decide to ease rates for the next commercial bank cash reserves period.

"The Bank of Portugal won't touch anything. The market is short of liquidity and we want to see what April inflation looks like and whether currency markets will settle at these levels," said Joao Miguel Lourenca at brokers Siemca.
"Against this background it would be premature to cut rates since we don't know what the FED is going to do."

Another analyst who declined to be named said: "The conditions are right for easing. The escudo is strong, rates are low everywhere and the market has already discounted a cut. But it is too soon since they last cut rates."

The Bank of Portugal last trimmed rates on April 11 when it took 20 basis points off the repo rate to leave it at 6.30 percent and 40 off the drain rate which now stands at 5.80 percent. Its emergency rate for one-day funds is 7.80 percent.
The Bank is due to announce its terms for the new period, which begins on Monday, at 1315 GMT on Friday.
"I think the main reason for not altering the rates is the inflation number. As far as the escudo is concerned, they could come down," said Isabel Costa at Banco Finantia.
The escudo had risen to around 100.20 per mark earlier this week from around 100.60 at the end of March before slipping back today to 100.30.

Analysts expect year-on-year inflation, which stood at 2.5 percent in March, to fall to or below two percent in April and May as meat prices, which surged last year on the mad cow scare, drop out of the index.

Some analysts said that French political uncertainty since the announcement of early elections there next month might inhibit any rate move in Portugal because the escudo is vulnerable to franc volatility.
Others thought the Bank of Portugal might even want to wait to see if the Federal Reserve raises short-term U.S. rates at its Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.
